description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 未提交变更整理与规范提交（项目周期外的实用指令）。当用户请求整理并规范提交未提交的改动，或调用 moma-commit 指令时使用本技能， 一键分析 git 工作区的全部未提交变更，区分为"有用的改动""应被版本控制忽略的文件""无意义文件（如空文件）""疑似敏感文件"四类； 有用的改动按逻辑意图分组为多个规范提交，呈现计划并经用户确认后执行；无意义文件不提交也不删除，结束时列出清单提醒用户手动清除。 本指令不修改任何业务代码内容，不推送远端。

name: moma-discuss
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 想法讨论与可行性分析（项目周期外的实用指令）。当用户请求讨论一个想法的可行性，或调用 moma-discuss 指令时使用本技能， 围绕用户提出的想法开展结构化讨论：只读分析项目现状（代码结构、技术栈、既有文档），给出可行性结论， 列出候选方案并比较后推荐最优方案，对想法中不明确的细节主动提问澄清；讨论阶段不修改任何代码与既有文档。 讨论收敛并经用户明确准许后，按变更性质路由到对应的 /moma-* 变更流程（或轻量实施模式）继续执行。

name: moma-fix
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 异常修复。当用户请求修复代码异常，或调用 moma-fix 指令时使用本技能， 分析并修复用户描述的代码异常，输出问题原因说明，按 07-测试策略.md 的缺陷记录模板在 bugs/ 目录下新建 BUG-xxx.md 记录文件，并以 bug: 前缀格式生成版本控制提交。

name: moma-incident
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 事故应急。当用户请求应急处理生产事故，或调用 moma-incident 指令时使用本技能， 按"先止血、后定位、再修复防复发"三步处理生产事故：优先回滚或降级等可逆止血措施，再定位根因， 写入事故记录并将正式修复交 /moma-fix。紧急情况可先止血后补登记，但事后必须补齐。

name: moma-init
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 项目启动。当用户请求启动新项目并生成文档，或调用 moma-init 指令时使用本技能， 从用户的自然语言需求出发，按阶段1（需求定义）→ 阶段2（技术设计）→ 阶段3（开发约束）的顺序 生成全套项目文档（01~07），为后续 /moma-coding 编码做准备。本指令仅生成文档，不进入编码阶段。

name: moma-migrate
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 数据库迁移。当用户请求执行数据模型迁移，或调用 moma-migrate 指令时使用本技能， 执行数据模型变更的高危流程：先同步更新 04-数据模型文档，再生成可回滚的迁移脚本与回滚方案， 确认备份并获用户逐项授权后执行，执行后验证数据。物理删除数据必须获用户明确确认。

name: moma-modify
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 需求调整。当用户请求调整已有需求，或调用 moma-modify 指令时使用本技能， 调整已有需求（含功能删减）并同步更新 01/02 文档及受影响的下游文档，随后按需进行代码变更， 在 changes/ 目录下新建变更记录文件，并以 modify: 前缀格式生成版本控制提交。

name: moma-new
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 功能新增。当用户请求新增一个功能，或调用 moma-new 指令时使用本技能， 增加原有需求中未描述的全新功能，定位归属模块后同步更新 01/02 及受影响的下游文档， 按需进行代码变更，在 changes/ 目录下新建变更记录文件，并以 feat: 前缀格式生成版本控制提交。

name: moma-optimize
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 功能优化。当用户请求细化或优化已有功能，或调用 moma-optimize 指令时使用本技能， 对已有需求进行更详细的约束和优化（细化现有功能的行为边界，而非新增功能），同步更新 01/02 及受影响的下游文档， 按需进行代码变更，在 changes/ 目录下新建变更记录文件，并以 optimize: 前缀格式生成版本控制提交。 也支持纯重构模式：外部行为不变时跳过文档更新。

name: moma-release
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 版本发布。当用户请求发布一个新版本，或调用 moma-release 指令时使用本技能， 聚合 changes/ 与 bugs/ 目录中自上一个 tag 以来的记录文件生成发布说明（releases/ 目录）， 更新项目工程版本号，并在用户确认后生成 release 提交与 tag。本指令不修改业务逻辑代码。

name: moma-retro
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 项目复盘。当用户请求对项目做复盘，或调用 moma-retro 指令时使用本技能， 对项目或里程碑进行复盘：聚合会话归档、变更日志、缺陷记录与版本历史，生成复盘报告 （目标达成、过程数据、经验教训、可落地的改进行动）到 retro-reports/ 目录。 本指令不修改代码与 01~07 文档。

name: moma-review
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 代码评审。当用户请求评审代码变更，或调用 moma-review 指令时使用本技能， 对照 01~07 文档与开发规约评审指定范围的代码变更，按阻断/严重/一般/建议分级输出问题清单， 评审记录写入 review-records/ 目录。本指令只读代码、只输出评审意见，不直接修改业务代码。

name: moma-security
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 安全审查。当用户请求做一次安全审查，或调用 moma-security 指令时使用本技能， 对指定范围进行注入、认证与授权、敏感信息、依赖漏洞、配置安全、数据保护六维度安全审查， 输出分级问题清单与安全报告到 security-reports/ 目录。本指令只读，不修改代码。

name: moma-session-complete
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 会话归档。当用户请求总结并归档当前会话，或调用 moma-session-complete 指令时使用本技能， 将当前会话的全过程进行结构化总结，并保存为 markdown 文档归档到与项目过程文档同根目录的 session-records/ 子目录下（即 dev-docs/session-records/）。本指令不修改业务代码与 01~07 文档。

name: moma-soft-dev
description: AI 驱动的简化软件开发流程管控总览技能，集中维护 moma-* 系列子技能的共享约定（文档存放规则、文档体系、编码通用约束、验证阶梯、文档预检规则）。 当用户询问 moma-soft-dev 流程的总体设计、文档体系、阶段划分，或不确定该用哪个 /moma-* 指令时使用本技能。 每个具体的工作指令由独立的子技能处理：/moma-init、/moma-sync、/moma-coding、/moma-modify、/moma-optimize、/moma-new、/moma-fix、/moma-test、/moma-review、/moma-check、/moma-release、/moma-incident、/moma-migrate、/moma-security、/moma-retro、/moma-session-complete、/moma-commit、/moma-discuss。 这些子技能均位于 skills/moma-* 目录下，并共享 skills/moma-soft-dev/references/common-conventions.md 中定义的约定。

name: moma-sync
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 项目同步 / 需求同步。当用户请求为已有项目补全或生成文档，或调用 moma-sync 指令时使用本技能， 针对已有代码的项目，通过分析现有代码反向补全或生成 01~07 文档体系，让后续的 AI 编码也能受到文档约束。 本指令仅生成/补全文档，不直接修改代码。

name: moma-test
description: moma-soft-dev 子技能 —— 测试验证。当用户请求补齐并执行测试，或调用 moma-test 指令时使用本技能， 依据 07-测试策略.md 补齐并执行测试，输出测试报告到 test-reports/ 目录，发现的缺陷按缺陷记录模板在 bugs/ 目录下新建 BUG 记录文件，并对状态为"已修复"的缺陷做回归验证后流转为"已验证"。 本指令只修改测试相关代码与记录文件，不修改业务代码。

name: momagraph-bench-eval
description: Evaluates embodied task planning and visual correspondence capabilities of vision-language models. It probes spatial-functional reasoning, multi-step action planning, and cross-view consistency in indoor scenes. Use when the user wants to benchmark on MomaGraph-Bench, BLINK, or asks about evaluating this task. Reports accuracy (%).

name: momap
description: Use when preparing, running, validating, or reporting licensed MOMAP photophysics workflows from Gaussian outputs, including EVC, vibronic spectra, and explicitly parameterized ISC calculations.

name: momapy
description: Build, read, write, modify, or render SBGN (Process Description / Activity Flow) and CellDesigner molecular maps with the momapy Python library. Trigger when a project imports `momapy`, when the user asks about the momapy API (Map / Model / Layout / `LayoutModelMapping`, frozen dataclasses, the builder pattern, `read()` / `write()`, rendering to SVG/PDF/PNG), or when working with `.sbgn`, `.sbgnml`, `.xml` (CellDesigner) files in a momapy context.

name: momen-baas

name: momen-cursurrules-prompt-file
description: Cursor rules for building custom frontends with Momen.app as headless BaaS with GraphQL API, actionflows, AI agents, and Stripe integration.

name: momen-platform
description: Orientation and entry point for working on a Momen project. Load first for any Momen app task — designing or changing the data model, UI, server-side action flows, permissions, payments, or data bindings, or reading runtime logs — then follow it to the right capability. For Momen projects only; not generic programming help.

name: moment
description: Operate Moment, the family timeline, over HTTP: chains, moments, feed, comments, media, share links, search, and monthly recaps. Use when the user mentions Moment, 时刻, 时光链, 那年今日, 月度回顾, or runs /moment. Call catalog endpoints with the user's personal access token; do not invent APIs.

name: moment-campus
description: 此刻校园是一个面向高校学生的实时生活分享与发现平台。本 Skill 提供浏览、搜索、发布、互动、话题、地图等核心能力，帮助用户在小程序 AI 对话中完成校园生活相关的信息获取与操作。

name: moment-capture
description: Capture the player's felt reactions to play verbatim into an append-only docs/moments.md, at the time they happen. Use whenever someone reports an aesthetic, emotional, or semantic reaction to playing — 'feels chunky', 'that's satisfying', 'this doesn't read right', 'I stopped watching', 'attack timing is unclear'. Positive reactions matter as much as negative ones. Felt reactions decay fast and get rationalised on recall, so the verbatim record beats a reconstruction. Not for bug reports, feature requests, or performance complaints — those belong in the tracker. For designing a structured se…

name: moment-craft
description: Recipes for the four Role Prep moment kinds — know-cold, question, pushback and challenge — including how to plan a sub-topic's series and how to write pushback options without giveaways. Load when planning or writing moments, or reviewing pushbacks.

name: moment-datetime
description: 日期时间工具，提供 dayjs 风格的 Moment 链式值类型（StartOf/EndOf/Add/Sub/Diff）、紧凑格式化与解析、柔性日期解析、时区换算、工作日与月末计算、年龄计算与计时器；当需要日期截断、区间计算、多格式日期解析或耗时统计时使用

name: moment-finder
description: Find the best clip moments in a long video, stream VOD or local file. Use when the user gives a YouTube URL or video file and wants highlights, "find the moments", or candidates to cut.

name: moment-finder
description: Find the top 3 highlight moments in an analysed video from loudness spikes, scene-cut density and letterbox detection, with lead-in context before each payoff. Use after ingest-probe when the user wants highlights or the best moments.

name: moment-inertia
description: Moment of Inertia in Mechanics (Rotation). Theoretical foundations, governing equations, analytical problem-solving methods, and typical archetypes.

name: moment-nulling-constraint-configuration
description: Use when designing MRI gradient waveforms that must null specific gradient moments (flow/velocity, acceleration, or higher-order motion compensation) subject to hardware limits (Gmax, slew) and optionally a Schulte et al PNS threshold, e.g. phase-contrast flow-encoding gradients.

name: moment-of-being-capture
description: Find and articulate the luminous moments within ordinary experience where meaning becomes visible—the breaks in "cotton wool" when pattern reveals itself.

name: moment-plan-generator
description: 将 Markdown 文案、聊天记录或已确认的朋友圈内容文档，可视化为可交互的 HTML 页面，支持多风格模板、自动日期跳转、一键复制和防折叠混淆。

name: moment-reel
description: Make a 30-50 second vertical cartoon story reel of a famous sports moment (a goal, a buzzer beater, a knockout) - a flat 2D cartoon with bold colours, thick outlines and expressive faces, freezes on the key instant, 2-4 word burned-in captions and a free local voice-over - with every fact checked first, rendered to a 1080x1920 master and a 7:8 X cut under 10 MB. Use when the user asks to rebuild, recreate, animate, cartoon or "make a reel of" a famous sports moment, goal, play, shot or fight, or types /moment-reel.

name: moment-research
description: Daily DuberyMNL "Moment Scout" — research upcoming PH holidays, sports/events, and viral/weather moments relevant to sunglasses, score them, write a sunglasses angle, write suggestions to the content calendar, and send the morning Telegram digest. Suggest-only; RA approves angles. Run daily (cloud routine / Task Scheduler) or on demand.

name: moment-router
description: Classifies the current client message into one of 7 messaging moments, then hands off to the right moment-specific skill. Runs first in the qa-handling pipeline.

name: moment-to-meaning
description: Turn everyday experiences, rough anecdotes, flat reports, speech memories, and business examples into vivid, useful spoken stories with Vinh Giang's three ingredients: specificity, reliving rather than reporting, and audience-relevant meaning. Use for meeting stories, presentations, interviews, customer examples, leadership communication, Toastmasters speeches, story coaching, or deciding whether a story will improve a message or get in the way; especially when a story feels generic, detached, overly descriptive, pointless, or disconnected from what the audience should understand or do.

name: momenta-misinformation-eval
description: Evaluates a multimodal misinformation detection model's ability to classify fake vs. real news across heterogeneous datasets, measuring classification accuracy, ranking quality, and class-balanced performance under calibrated decision thresholds. Use when the user wants to benchmark on Fakeddit, MMCoVaR, Weibo, XFacta, or asks about evaluating this task. Reports F1.

name: momenta-multimodal-moe-misinformation-detection
description: MOMENTA — Mixture-of-Experts over multimodal embeddings with neural temporal aggregation for misinformation detection. Combines modality-specific MoE modules, bidirectional co-attention, discrepancy-aware branch, and attention-based temporal aggregation with drift/momentum encoding. Use when: multimodal misinformation detection, MoE for multimodal learning, temporal aggregation, cross-modal disagreement detection, fact-checking systems. Trigger: misinformation detection, multimodal MoE, cross-modal disagreement, temporal drift, fake news detection, MOMENTA, 多模态虚假信息检测.

name: momente-finder

Liefert eine Liste mit Zeitstempeln und Grund. Nutze ihn, wenn der Nutzer sagt "finde die besten Stellen", "was ist clipbar", "Highlights im VOD", "Momente suchen" oder einen VOD-Link gibt.

description: Diagnose and classify failing Momentic browser, Android, and iOS tests, compare run history, and repair quarantined tests.

name: momentive

Covers scaffolding, deploying, invoking, the example patterns (proxies, token vending, vector search, event handlers), and debugging memory limits and wasm panics. name: moonweave-flow

name: moonweave-gap-analysis
description: Compare the project's current facts against Moonweave governance requirements, identify missing Owners, decisions, tests, docs, risk reviews, automation, handoffs, and runtime evidence, and convert repeated manual corrections into rules, skills, CI, or templates. name: moonweave-gap-analysis

name: moonweave-gap-analysis

name: moonweave-governance-change

name: moonweave-governance-change

name: moonweave-governance-change

Used to update the governance repository, add/modify a skill, or adapt platform adapters.

name: moonweave-governance-router

name: moonweave-governance-router

description: 在实现适配器前对候选模型做分析。确定模型实现来源（transformers / 模型目录 / diffusers）、结构特征、内存约束下的逐层量化建议（可选）及 MoE 融合权重风险。适用于用户询问模型适配可行性或做适配前分析时使用。识别为 DiT 扩散模型时，索取推理仓路径后回传 `next_step: model-adapt`，由 orchestrator 委派 `msmodelslim-model-adapt`（DiT 扩展节承接）。

name: msmodelslim-model-analysis
description: 在实现适配器前对候选模型做分析。确定模型实现来源（transformers 或模型目录）、结构特征、内存约束下的逐层量化建议（可选）及 MoE 融合权重风险。适用于用户询问模型适配可行性或做适配前分析时使用。

name: msmodelslim-model-dequant
description: 为 msModelSlim 适配流程注入反量化能力。先识别模型权重是否可反量化，再实现反量化脚本并接入 model_adapter。当前仅覆盖 FP8 的 per-block 与 per-channel 两类；若格式不确定或无公开反量化规则，要求用户提供反量化脚本或浮点权重。

name: msmodelslim-quant
description: 华为昇腾 NPU 服务器模型quant工具技能，专为在昇腾 NPU 卡上进行大语言模型quant加速，聚焦于msmodelslim已验证模型的快速量化流程，支持量化流程和量化配置的轻微修改。支持 INT4/INT8/INT16 quant，提供完整的quant工作流，包括环境检查、动态方案query、容器deployment、quant执行等。

name: msmodelslim-quick-quant
description: 提供 msModelSlim 的通用快速量化指引，包含安装、最简 YAML 配置与基础执行校验。适用于用户询问 msmodelslim 安装、快速量化、配置 yaml、linear_quant 或 minmax 基础参数时。

name: msmq-built-in-connector
description: Rules for migrating BizTalk MSMQ and NetMsmq adapters to the Logic Apps Standard built-in MSMQ connector, including broker topology, workflow behavior, networking, delivery guarantees, and validation.

name: msms-atlas-lookup
description: Batch lookup predicted spectra by SMILES from a locally mounted ICEBERG atlas when that atlas is available.

name: msms-atlas-retrieval
description: Retrieve candidate structures for an experimental MS/MS spectrum from the public ICEBERG PubChem atlas. Use for formula-based or mass-based atlas searches; route direct model prediction and fingerprint comparison to their respective skills.

name: msms-atlas-to-ms
description: Convert atlas-lookup spectra (HDF5 from msms-atlas-lookup) into ms-pred's native .ms format, one file per molecule.

name: msms-based-compound-candidate-ranking
description: Use when feature groups retaining MS/MS peak lists and formula candidates (e.g. from GenForm/SIRIUS) need compound identification by ranking database candidates against MS/MS peaks.

name: msms-candidate-penalty-scoring
description: Use when you have MS/MS (or MSn) peak lists with a precursor elemental composition and need to rank candidate structures from a chemical database without reference spectra.

name: msms-clustering-parameter-sweep-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking tandem-MS clustering tools on untargeted metabolomics spectra (Orbitrap or qTof mzML/MGF) and you need purity/N10 trade-off curves across tool parameter settings rather than a single clustering run.

name: msms-confidence-score-modeling
description: Use when ranking top-k candidate molecular formulas generated from tandem mass spectra requires a learned confidence score, e.g. training a rescore model on Orbitrap or Q-TOF MS/MS features.

name: msms-cosine-similarity-evaluation
description: Use when a set of predicted MS/MS spectra (MGF/PKL from 3DMolMS or baselines) must be quantitatively scored against experimental Agilent Q-TOF PCDL/NIST20 spectra, per compound and per ion mode ([M+H]+, [M-H]-).

name: msms-cosine-similarity-fingerprinting
description: Use when a query MS/MS spectrum (reference spectrum from GNPS or a cryptic spectrum from a paired genome-MS/MS sample) must be converted into a similarity fingerprint so it can be matched to biosynthetic gene cluster families via the NPOmix KNN classifier.

name: msms-cosine-similarity-library-matching
description: Use when untargeted LC–MS/MS feature tables carry acquired MS2 spectra for a subset of features and you want per-annotation posterior probabilities that exploit the fragmentation pattern, not just MS1 peak masses and adducts.

name: msms-coverage-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when LC-HRMS/MS workflow needs to measure how many true chromatographic peaks receive MS/MS coverage before and after applying an exclusion list generated from background (wall) annotations, and the result must be compared against published baseline counts (Supplementary Table S2).

name: msms-dataset-batch-processing
description: Use when benchmarking formula assignment across multiple qualified MS/MS datasets — e.g. computing rank#1/top-3/top-5 accuracy and total processing time for SIRIUS, Buddy, or FSA on identical spectra and hardware.

name: msms-denovo
description: Generate formula-constrained structures from an experimental .ms spectrum with FRIGID when retrieval or direct model scoring leaves no satisfactory candidate.

name: msms-dereplication
description: Use when raw or identified tandem MS (MS/MS) data from public repositories (e.g., MassIVE) needs compound-level annotations via exact spectral library search, or when tracking identification growth across library updates ('living data' reanalysis).

name: msms-dilution-series-entropy-similarity-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing denoising algorithms (e.g. Spectral Denoising vs MS Reduce, 1% base-peak thresholding, DNL) on serial-dilution MS/MS data against ground-truth reference spectra, to measure annotation gains and false negatives.

name: msms-embedding-prediction
description: Use when annotating MSP-format MS/MS spectra (MSP files with or without SMILES) for a chosen polarity whose features have precursor masses and known adducts, and you need top-N candidate compound IDs from embeddings rather than spectral-library dot-product matching.

name: msms-entropy-similarity-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify agreement between a noisy/denoised query MS/MS spectrum and a clean reference spectrum (e.g., validating electronic+chemical denoising of .msp spectra) or to score spectral matches in Denoising Search.

name: msms-evidence-review
description: Assess ranked MS/MS candidates against matched and unexplained peaks across all supplied collision energies, and write evidence_review.json. Use after retrieval or scoring, including strong matches, empty candidate results and delegated per-feature reviews; route new structure proposals to msms-structure-proposal.

name: msms-exclusion-list-generation
description: Use when PeakBot has annotated walls/background signals in blank or background LC-HRMS samples and you need a targeted DDA exclusion list to boost MS/MS coverage of true chromatographic peaks in subsequent runs.

name: msms-feature-detect
description: Detect and align LC-MS features with GNPS2 Everything Bagel or local MZmine, then export feature MS/MS spectra for structure elucidation.

name: msms-feature-preprocessing
description: Use when a .mgf file of MS/MS feature spectra (e.g. wheat or urine metabolome LC–MS/MS with <1000–<4000 features) must be turned into a specXplore session data object with pairwise similarity matrices before t-SNE or dashboard exploration.

name: msms-fingerprint-compare
description: Compare MIST-predicted fingerprints against deterministic Morgan fingerprints for the same molecules via Tanimoto similarity.

name: msms-fingerprint-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when a study has MS/MS spectra left unannotated by spectral library search (e.g. IDSL.CSA vs NIST 20/LipidBlast) and you need to quantify annotation gains from predicted-fingerprint structure matching.

name: msms-formula-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you have ranked candidate molecular formulas per MS/MS spectrum (from FSA or a comparable ranker) and need to quantify rank#1 accuracy, top-5 accuracy, and per-spectrum runtime against known metabolite ground truth.

name: msms-fragment-annotation
description: Use when you need theoretical MS/MS fragment ions for derivatized unsaturated sterols (or other C=C-containing molecules) to support matching of LC-IM-MS/MS features against a reference lipid database.

name: msms-fragment-bag-of-words-corpus-construction
description: Use when raw MS2 spectra (e.g. from beer-extract or other complex-mixture LC-MS/MS runs) must be converted into the fragment-and-neutral-loss bag-of-words documents that LDA/MS2LDA topic modeling consumes.

name: msms-fragment-binning-and-factorization
description: Use when comparing MS/MS spectra of several features from an .mgf file to see which fragment m/z values and neutral losses they share in one heatmap view.

name: msms-fragment-data-extraction
description: Use when UNIFI-exported .xlsx MS/MS spectra of reference standards need to be converted into a fragment datatable stratified by standard and collision energy (20/40/60 eV).

name: msms-fragment-intensity-extraction
description: Use when quantifying histone peptides from Mascot .csv output by MS/MS total ion intensity, especially when composite spectra contain two isobaric peptides sharing the same sequence but distinct PTM localizations that must be deconvoluted.

name: msms-fragment-ion-overlap-quantification
description: Use when LC–MS/MS spectra (.mgf) are embedded via an ms2deepscore similarity matrix and you need to characterize how much of the fragmentation signal is shared among spectra in a dense local neighborhood around a feature of interest.

name: msms-fragment-ion-prediction
description: Use when public/commercial MS/MS libraries lack spectra for a compound class (e.g., <50 acylcarnitine structures) and MSI level 2 annotation requires predicted fragment ions.

name: msms-fragment-lfp-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you have chained MS/MS fragment ion-intensity profiles of two (or more) isomeric compounds across multiple collision energies and need per-fragment similarity scores to distinguish them.

name: msms-fragment-library-generation
description: Reference for building or extending metabolite fragment libraries when new experimental MS/MS spectra (e.g. MassBank records such as MSBNK-RIKEN-PR100295 for Pantothenic acid [M+H]+) must be converted into scored .csv entries for MetaboAnnotatoR.

name: msms-fragment-library-searching
description: Use when an aligned feature table contains m/z and retention-time pairs whose monoisotopic precursor masses need compound-level annotation via MS/MS spectral matching against an online MassBank library.

name: msms-fragment-mass-enumeration
description: Use when building targeted PRM/MRM or DIA assays for lipids and you must enumerate precursor-to-fragment transitions (m/z, adduct, charge) for lipid classes rather than measuring them experimentally.

name: msms-fragment-overlap-analysis
description: Decision support for whether CFM-ID predicted fragments can back annotation of DNA adducts in HRMS adductomics when experimental MS/MS spectra exist only for a subset (e.g. 15 of 582) of database entries.

name: msms-fragment-pattern-search
description: Use when you have centroided LC/MS data (mzML) with a feature table and MS2 scans, and a known diagnostic product ion (e.g., m/z 333.0592) to screen for structurally related features across many spectra.

name: msms-fragment-peak-matching
description: Use when annotating an LC-MS/MS peak (e.g. negative-mode peak M386T77, m/z 385.1118, RT 1.27 min) by matching its fragment peaks to a candidate metabolite's reference fragments within a 10 ppm tolerance to obtain an MS/MS score.

name: msms-fragment-profile-matching
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS data are acquired at multiple collision energies (e.g., stepped NCE 20/40/60%) and isomers with similar substructures must be distinguished, so a single cross-sectional spectrum match is insufficient.

name: msms-fragment-screening
description: Use when a blank-filtered LC-HRMS/MS feature table (e.g. AFFF samples) needs PFAS candidate flagging via MS/MS fragment matching, especially for precursor ions whose exact masses match nothing in the EPA catalogued PFAS list.

name: msms-fragment-simulation-for-n-me-derivatized-sterols
description: Use when building a spectral library or 4D identification database for N-Me derivatized unsaturated sterol lipids, and theoretical fragment ions matching N-Me fragmentation patterns are needed for LC-IM-MS/MS annotation.

name: msms-fragmentation-candidate-ranking
description: Use when a challenge provides MS/MS peak lists (possibly merged across collision energies) with a known elemental composition, and candidate structures must be retrieved from PubChem and ranked without reference spectra.

name: msms-fragmentation-depth-sweep
description: Use when you need to assess how deeply MAGMa breadth-first fragmentation (depth 2 vs 3 vs 4) affects ModiFinder's shifted-peak annotation coverage and MF-O evaluation scores on an MS/MS analog pair benchmark.

name: msms-fragmentation-pattern-annotation
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network (MS/MS spectra as vertices, modified-cosine edges) must be interpreted by mapping mineMS2-mined fragmentation patterns onto its components and exporting for Cytoscape.

name: msms-fragmentation-pattern-matching-to-network-components
description: Use when you have a mined mineMS2 pattern library plus a GNPS molecular network (components of similar MS/MS spectra) and need to identify which patterns specifically explain each network component.

name: msms-hypergeometric-score-histogram-analysis
description: Use when you have per-feature MS/MS spectral match scores from searching lipid annotations against two or more spectral libraries (e.g., CalicoLipids vs MS-DIAL) and need library-specific score cutoffs to separate authentic from spurious identifications.

name: msms-inspect
description: Interactive TIC/MS1/MS2 chromatogram viewer for mzML files; lets you browse retention time, inspect precursor masses, and export individual spectra as .ms files.

name: msms-intensity-coincidence-analysis
description: Use when calibrating an electronic-noise removal threshold for MS/MS spectra: you need to empirically justify how many ions per spectrum can share near-identical relative intensities (±0.1%) before denoising experimental Orbitrap data.

name: msms-intensity-coverage-filtering
description: Use when curating raw MS/MS spectral libraries (NIST'17, MS-DIAL, MSnLib .mgf/.msp entries) into training-ready data for in silico fragmentation models and uncurated spectra must be quality-controlled by fragment-to-peak matching criteria.

name: msms-intensity-normalization-to-unit-sum
description: Use when a centroided MS/MS spectrum has been cleaned (peaks merged within +/- 0.05 Da, noise-filtered) and you need intensities as a probability distribution for spectral entropy or entropy-similarity calculations.

name: msms-intensity-weighting
description: Use when a centroided, normalized MS/MS peak list must be intensity-weighted prior to entropy similarity computation and the spectrum's entropy (or ion richness) is unknown or low (S < 3).

name: msms-library-count-verification
description: Use when a deposited MS/MS reference library (MGF or matchms-readable format) carries reported totals of spectra and unique compounds that must be independently verified against the Zenodo archive before downstream use or benchmarking.

name: msms-library-matching
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS feature tables from lipidomics experiments (e.g. Thermo .raw, SCIEX .wiff, .mzML inputs) need MS2 library-search annotation against a theoretical spectral library covering lipid chain compositions and C=C double-bond positions.

name: msms-longitudinal-fragment-profiling-scoring
description: Use when annotating metabolites from MS/MS spectra acquired at multiple distinct collision energies (e.g., stepped NCE 20/40/60%) and you need per-candidate similarity ranking plus ROC-derived identification thresholds.

name: msms-metadata-harmonization
description: Use when a raw or merged MS/MS spectral library in MGF format contains inconsistent metadata fields, missing precursor m/z or ionization mode, or annotations whose parent mass/adduct contradict the precursor m/z and SMILES.

name: msms-mist-fingerprint
description: Predict molecular fingerprints from MS/MS spectra using only FRIGID's MIST encoder, skipping diffusion generation and ICEBERG refinement.

name: msms-modified-cosine-similarity-scoring
description: Use when building the testing matrix of MS/MS fingerprints for NPOmix KNN classification — i.e., when you have query reference spectra (e.g., 15 GNPS reference spectra) and paired samples with merged experimental spectra, and need per-sample maximum modified cosine similarity scores.

name: msms-modified-cosine-spectral-matching
description: Use when you have paired genome–metabolome samples (PoDP-style, e.g. the 1,040-sample GNPS job task=b915d1f78c364bf4be9900047760d95c) and reference or cryptic MS/MS spectra that must be converted into similarity fingerprints for BGC–metabolite linking.

name: msms-molecular-networking
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS metabolomics files (e.g. mzML/MassIVE MSV000083738) must be grouped into molecular families to identify analogues of known metabolites such as detoxins and rimosamides.

name: msms-multiple-spectral-alignment-across-molecular-family
description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra grouped into a GNPS2 molecular network component (or a set of USIs) and need to see which peaks align across all spectra — including shifted analog peaks like rhamnolipid HAA fragments (m/z 211.130 vs 239.

name: msms-neutral-loss-annotation
description: Use when a filtered feature table contains a candidate metabolite feature (e.g. m/z 185.1183) whose identity must be supported by MS/MS evidence such as a diagnostic neutral loss before accepting it in the final metabolite set.

name: msms-neutral-loss-interpretation
description: Use when interpreting ICEBERG fragment attribution outputs — e.g., after running predict_smis.py on held-out molecules — to check whether breakage frequencies and hydrogen shifts match chemistry intuition (C-O/C-N favored over C-C; -1H ↔ H2O loss).

name: msms-noise-denoising
description: Use when raw MS/MS query spectra (e.g., AD plasma from Orbitrap Astral or Exploris 240) contain electronic and chemical noise ions, and the goal is higher-confidence compound annotation via spectral library matching with entropy similarity.

name: msms-noise-filtering
description: Use when raw MS2 fragmentation spectra paired to MS1 peaks contain noisy fragment or neutral-loss entries that must be removed before building a bag-of-fragments matrix or running topic-model inference.

name: msms-noise-ion-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking MS/MS library-matching similarity scores for robustness: you have cleaned, centroided reference spectra and need to quantify score degradation as artificial noise ions are added at graded levels.

name: msms-pairwise-similarity-computation
description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra (MGF files) from a spectral library or extract library and need pairwise similarity scores that reflect structural relatedness, e.g., to build a molecular network or find structural analogues beyond cosine-based matching.

name: msms-pattern-interpretation
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network component or spectral cluster needs a chemical interpretation, and MS/MS spectra (e.g., LC-HRMS .mgf with metadata) can be mined for shared, graph-structured m/z differences.

name: msms-peak-filtering
description: Use when raw MS/MS peak sets from spectra in a molecular network component must be preprocessed before MMSA multiple spectral alignment, e.g. to reduce noise and outlier intensity effects prior to consensus peak identification.

name: msms-peak-formula-annotation-matching
description: Use when comparing predicted formula annotations against expert-curated peak annotations on held-out MS/MS spectra (e.g., NIST20 scaffold-split test set) to score formula-level agreement of C2MS models such as FraGNNet, GrAFF-MS, or ICEBERG.

name: msms-peak-fragment-matching
description: Use when you have a measured HR-MS/MS peak list and a set of candidate structures, and need to rank candidates by how well their in silico fragments explain the product ions.

name: msms-peak-intensity-coverage-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify how much of the total peak intensity of real MS/MS spectra (e.g., NIST20, [M+H]+, HCD Orbitrap) is explained by an approximate fragmentation DAG with given depth d and hydrogen tolerance j.

name: msms-peak-list-extraction
description: Use when a raw MS/MS spectrum loaded from an MGF file must have low relative-intensity peaks removed via matchms, and you need the retained and filtered-out peak lists for inspection.

name: msms-peak-list-format-conversion
description: Use when raw MS/MS contest or experiment peak lists (precursor m/z plus fragment m/z-intensity pairs, possibly at several collision energies) must be restructured into MAGMa hierarchical input files before in silico candidate annotation.

name: msms-peak-list-processing
description: Use when LC-MS/MS runs in mzML or mzXML format must be converted into cleaned, feature-merged peak lists feeding molecular formula determination or structure annotation with SIRIUS 4 / COSMIC.

name: msms-peak-list-scoring
description: Use when open mass spectral library records (.MSP/.MGF/.JSON/.CSV/.XML) contain inconsistent, oversized, or low-information peak lists that must be cleaned and scored before library integration or MS/MS annotation in MS-Dial.

name: msms-peak-post-processing-filtering
description: Use when a predicted ESI-MS/MS peak list (CFM-ID 4.0/3.0/2.0 output at 10, 20, 40 eV) must be trimmed to a canonical form before comparing against experimental Metlin QTOF spectra with peak-match metrics.

name: msms-peak-presence-thresholding
description: Use when reconstructing in silico MS/MS spectra from candidate SMILES with SingleFrag: for each of the most frequented MZ positions, an ANN prediction must be converted into a binary peak call via a position-specific threshold.

name: msms-peak-substructure-matching
description: Use when annotating unknown fragment ion spectra solely from candidate structures in the absence of reference spectra, e.g. ranking PubChem candidates for LC-MS metabolite identification challenges.

name: msms-precursor-formula-ranking
description: Use when a precursor ion's molecular formula must be ranked from an LC-MS/MS spectrum using fragment peak masses and a PubChem-derived formula list, without MS/MS databases or trained models.

name: msms-precursor-fragment-association
description: Use when processing high-dimensional LC-IMS-MS/MS data where MS2 fragment ions must be attributed to MS1 precursors, especially when retention time alone is insufficient to separate coeluting species and drift time must be jointly considered.

name: msms-precursor-mass-filtering
description: Use when cleaning raw MS/MS spectra prior to formula identification — e.g., converting m/z to monoisotopic Da via adduct correction and removing spurious precursor-adjacent and contamination peaks.

name: msms-precursor-mass-matching
description: Use when MS/MS spectra from untargeted metabolomics have no level 1 hit from an authentic-standard library and you need MSI level 2 annotations from public or in-silico spectral libraries without retention time confirmation.

name: msms-predict
description: Predict MS/MS spectra and fragment assignments from SMILES with GLACIER or ICEBERG, and score supplied candidate structures against experimental spectra.

name: msms-preprocess
description: Convert raw instrument files (.raw, .d, etc.) to mzML or MGF for downstream model input; no-op if the file is already in a supported format.

name: msms-product-ion-intensity-normalization
description: Use when assessing day-to-day MS/MS product ion consistency from DDA-acquired system suitability (SST) data where stochastic precursor triggering makes raw product ion intensities incomparable across scans and acquisitions.

name: msms-product-ion-quantification
description: Use when LC-MS/MS mzML data (e.g., deuterated acylcarnitine SST mixture from MassIVE MSV000098825) must be queried for specific product ion intensities or neutral-loss signals across NCE steps and activation modes (CID vs HCD).

name: msms-query-spectrum-processing
description: Use when MS/MS query spectra from an annotated molecular network (GNPS/MassIVE) need per-spectrum molecular formula and structure identification, or when benchmarking a new annotation method against SIRIUS.

name: msms-retention-score-integration
description: Use when candidate lists from MS/MS tools (SIRIUS, MS-DIAL) for LC-MS peaks in an RPLC run need re-ranking with predicted retention-order scores, or when peaks lack usable MS/MS spectra.

name: msms-scan-retention-time-filtering
description: Use when processing ddMS2-topN or AIF UHPLC-HRMS/MS .ms2 files after MS1 exact-mass matching: you need to isolate the tandem-MS scans co-eluting with each feature before matching experimental fragments against in silico library m/z values.

name: msms-scan-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when a feature table row has multiple lipid candidates passing rule-based identification (same or similar m/z, co-eluting) and you must rank them by summed fragment intensity across MS/MS scans spanning the feature peak.

name: msms-scan-to-peak-group-assignment
description: Use when processing LC-MS/MS metabolomics or lipidomics mzML samples where fragmentation scans must be grouped into precursor-defined (m/z, RT) slices and attached to finalized peak groups rather than analyzed per-scan.

name: msms-search-result-file-parsing
description: Use when X!Tandem XML output files (e.g. from thegpm.org search engine) must be read programmatically to extract identifications, or when parsing-time/memory performance of search-result parsers is being benchmarked.

name: msms-search-score-interpretation
description: Use when input is an X!Tandem XML result file and you need per-spectrum identification details (peptide sequence, modified sequence, E-value, hyperscore, protein accession, charge, precursor and fragment m/z) exported for scoring interpretation.

name: msms-setup
description: Install these skills, configure local, SSH, Slurm or Kubernetes prediction servers, tune each model host in configs/local.yaml, and register the MCP server. Use when asked to install or set up the skills, or when model hosts change.

name: msms-shifted-peak-alignment-analysis
description: Use when two structurally related MS/MS spectra (MS2-known and MS2-unknown) are available with a 2D structure of the known compound, and the goal is to localize where the structural modification occurs on the known molecule.

name: msms-similarity-network-cluster-visualization
description: Use when exploring LC-MS/MS .mgf feature spectra with specXplore and you want cluster groupings (at several k values) of features based on ms2deepscore similarities, not edge-threshold-driven partial networks.

name: msms-similarity-network-propagation
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS peak table and MS2 spectra contain library-confirmed known metabolites and reaction-paired unknown peaks that must be annotated by propagating known seeds across spectrally similar, knowledge-guided network edges.

name: msms-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you have per-sample MS-DIAL feature lists (precursor MS1 m/z, RT, MS/MS spectra) from many samples (e.g. 545 wild soybean accessions) and need to align and merge equivalent features into one table.

name: msms-spectra-annotation
description: Use when experimental HR-MS/MS spectra (MGF) must be classified into user-defined substance classes, e.g. prioritizing putative (prenylated) flavonoids in natural product discovery.

name: msms-spectra-binning-and-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra (MoNA or NIST 17, positive mode, HCD/QqQ/Q-TOF or IT) must be preprocessed into binned, denoised feature vectors to train a multi-class multi-label ANN like MetFID.

name: msms-spectra-canopus-class-prediction
description: Use when per-spectrum or molecular-family-level chemical class annotations (ClassyFire/NPClassifier at super-, class-, and subclass-levels) are needed from MS/MS spectra in an NPLinker workflow and compounds are below 850 Da.

name: msms-spectra-compound-class-prediction
description: Use when experimental HR-MS/MS spectra (MGF files) must be screened against a user-defined 'relevant' substance class (e.g. prenylated flavonoids) for prioritization, and you have curated 'relevant' and 'other' reference spectra to train classifiers.

name: msms-spectra-csv-ingestion
description: Use when you have four comma-separated CSV peak lists of MS/MS spectra — [M+H]+ and [M-H]- at 35% and 130% NCE, with m/z in column 1 and intensity in column 2 — and need spectra embeddings for downstream structure decoding.

name: msms-spectra-database-searching
description: Use when LC-MS/MS spectra of metabolites or other small molecules must be identified at the structure level by searching a molecular structure database such as PubChem, and measured spectral-library matching (e.g. GNPS library cosine search) is insufficient or unavailable.

name: msms-spectra-export-mgf-mat
description: Use when detected LC-MS features have associated MS/MS spectra and you need portable spectral files (MGF/MAT) for GNPS spectral-library dereplication, MS-FINDER, or Sirius annotation.

name: msms-spectra-library-curation
description: Use when a local, self-contained reference compound/MS2 spectral database (e.g. SQLite CompDb) must be created from a public resource like HMDB so experimental fragment spectra can later be compared against a curated library.

name: msms-spectra-merging
description: Use when tandem MS/MS spectra must be converted into merged training feature vectors for per-bit libSVM fingerprint prediction, and candidate compounds must be ranked by Jaccard similarity of predicted vs. reference fingerprints from chemdb.

name: msms-spectra-merging-and-renormalization
description: Use when two centroided MS/MS peak lists (m/z, intensity) must be combined into a merged spectrum AB to compute spectral entropy similarity, e.g. for library matching or compound identification scoring.

name: msms-spectra-merging-by-inchikey

name: nanopore-long-read-isoform-alignment
description: Use when quantifying isoforms or PSI from single-cell/spatially barcoded Nanopore long reads (e.g., CRCLM sample) and raw minimap2 alignments show misaligned small internal exons inflating false-positive isoforms.

name: nanopore-long-read-locus-subsetting
description: Use when you need locus-restricted RNA editing or SNV rates from ScNaUmi-seq error-corrected consensus molecules, e.g. measuring A-to-I editing at two linked sites like Gria2 Q/R and R/G and testing whether editing at one site influences the other.

name: nanopore-long-read-methylation-pipeline
description: Use when analyzing EMseq/nanoEM base-converted Oxford Nanopore long reads to quantify per-CpG methylation genome-wide, or when reproducing methylation rates and CpG coverage versus WGBS, EMseq, and nanopolish.

name: nanopore-long-read-scaffolding-realtime
description: Use when a SPAdes short-read draft assembly needs finishing with nanopore long reads, especially when streaming MinION data in real time or when minimizing long-read coverage (e.g. ~30-fold for E. coli, ~14-fold for Kpn2146 plasmids).

name: nanopore-long-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking or validating long-read isoform quantification pipelines where real data lack gold-standard isoform counts, and a simulated cell-by-isoform matrix with known error profiles is needed as ground truth.

name: nanopore-long-read-to-short-read-conversion
description: Use when a nanopore FASTQ (e.g., .fq.gz from ONT) must be converted into NGS-liked short-read sets to run conventional NGS pipelines for hotspot mutation detection in a hotspot panel.

name: nanopore-m6a-per-read-classification
description: Use when ONT fastq/fast5 reads (Albacore-basecalled, R9/R9.4/R9.5) need per-read m6A probability calls at known motif or positions-file sites, using nanopolish eventalign TSVs with --scale-events and a trained model like r95_twobase_model_NN_6_m6A.pkl.

name: nanopore-metagenome-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking an ARG profiler (e.g., Argo) against assembly/metaFlye+Kraken2 or binning/SemiBin2+GTDB-Tk pipelines and ground-truth ARG abundances at controlled sequencing coverages are needed.

name: nanopore-metagenomic-classification-verification
description: Use when a real-time Oxford Nanopore (MinION/Flongle) metagenomic run has been classified with Kraken2 and hits to user-defined species of interest or pathogens need secondary confirmation before alerting.

name: nanopore-methylation
description: This page used to hold an archived copy of this skill. The archive now lives in the registry's data repository.

name: nanopore-methylation-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating methylation-calling accuracy of a Nanopore 5mC caller against short-read bisulfite ground truth at per-read and per-site granularity, needing stratified F1 scores with explicit methylation-frequency filters.

name: nanopore-methylation-calling
description: Use when calling 5mC methylation from ONT R10.4 POD5/BAM plant nanopore data in CpG, CHG, or CHH contexts, or when needing per-site methylation rates comparable to BS-seq across species.

name: nanopore-methylation-calling
description: Use when raw nanopore fast5 files must be converted to per-read 5mC CpG calls or per-site methylation frequencies, especially to benchmark or combine tool predictions on R9.4.1 flowcell data.

name: nanopore-methylation-feature-handling
description: Use when raw Nanopore FAST5 signals must be turned into balanced, denoised training samples for 5mC detection (e.g. building DeepSignal-plant training sets with CpG/CHG/CHH motifs from re-squiggled reads).

name: nanopore-methylation-motif-enrichment
description: Use when you need to de novo discover DNA methylation motifs (6mA, 5mC, 4mC) from native vs WGA nanopore signal data of a bacterium, and benchmark recovery against REBASE reference motifs.

name: nanopore-mock-community-diversity-analysis
description: Use when assessing whether direct 97% VSEARCH clustering of full-length post-chopSeq nanopore amplicon reads gives accurate OTU richness for mock communities, or when justifying a partition-based clustering step by quantifying singleton-driven OTU inflation.

name: nanopore-modification-calling-with-deepbam
description: Use when nanopore R10.4 FASTQ/BAM/POD5 data need CpG methylation calling and per-site modification rates, especially when Dorado's methylation model shows inconsistent performance across heterogeneous human or plant datasets.

name: nanopore-modification-frequency-filtering
description: Use when you have an aligned nanopore modBAM with MM/ML base-modification tags from direct RNA, cDNA, or genomic DNA reads and need high-confidence per-site modification calls filtered by coverage and modification frequency.

name: nanopore-modification-tool-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how accurately nanopore RNA modification callers (m6A/m5C) estimate site-level stoichiometry or sensitivity/FDR on known ground-truth mixtures, e.g. IVT sets with 20-100% modification levels.

name: nanopore-modified-basecalling
description: Use when raw Nanopore fast5 single-read files must be converted into per-read or per-site CpG 5mC methylation calls, or when comparing methylation-calling tools against a WGBS/truth reference.

name: nanopore-motif-typing-evaluation
description: Use when running Nanoident inference on bacterial Nanopore motif data and predicted methylation type (4mC/5mC/6mA) does not match the nucleotide at the predicted methylated position, requiring correction before accuracy evaluation.

name: nanopore-native-rna-read-classification
description: Use when you have native RNA Nanopore reads from a subcellular fraction (e.g. chromatin, nucleoplasm, cytoplasm) and need per-read premature vs. mature labels to estimate processing-state fractions.

name: nanopore-probability-distribution-modeling
description: Use when you have CHEUI-solo Model 1 per-read probability distributions grouped by transcript site and need site-level m6A/m5C modification probability and stoichiometry in a single condition without a knock-out/control sample.

name: nanopore-raw-data-file-parsing
description: Use when you need to enumerate every read stored in a POD5 file and extract each read's read_id, e.g. to build a read inventory, feed a filter list, or verify the number of reads a viewer reports.

name: nanopore-raw-signal-alignment
description: Use when performing signal-domain mapping of raw nanopore reads (BLOW5/FAST5) against a reference FASTA for selective sequencing (Read Until) or when benchmarking sDTW alignment throughput on CPU vs FPGA hardware.

name: nanopore-raw-signal-basecalling
description: Use when you have raw nanopore FAST5 electrolytic-current signal files and need to decode them into per-read nucleotide sequences without prior signal segmentation.

name: nanopore-raw-signal-basecalling
description: Use when raw nanopore fast5 files must be translated into basecalled reads (FASTQ/FASTA) with a deep learning basecaller, either with a pretrained model (DNA_default/RNA_default) or a custom-trained model, and accuracy should rival Albacore v2.0.1.

name: nanopore-raw-signal-event-detection
description: Use when raw nanopore signal reads (e.g., SARS-CoV-2 BLOW5 from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7314838) must be converted into per-read event sequences—event detection, prefix trimming, z-score normalization, and scaling—before squiggle mapping or sDTW-based Read Until on R9.4 chemistry.

name: nanopore-raw-signal-kmer-feature-encoding
description: Use when resquiggled Nanopore DRS FAST5 signals and basecall alignments are available and per-read k-mer/signal/error features must be encoded and pooled into site-level m6A probabilities.

name: nanopore-raw-signal-mapping
description: Use when the input is raw nanopore signal data (FAST5, POD5, SLOW5, or BLOW5) from legacy r9.4 chemistry that must be mapped to a reference genome in real time, especially for large genomes such as human NA12878.

name: nanopore-raw-signal-resquiggling
description: Use when preparing Nanopore DRS FAST5 reads for RedNano feature extraction: after guppy basecalling (--fast5_out) and before extracting k-mer raw signals, the signals must be resquiggled against a reference transcript FASTA.

name: nanopore-raw-signal-seed-hash-matching
description: Use when mapping raw nanopore signal reads to a reference genome via hash-based seed matching, or when reproducing how RawHash converts matching seed hash values into a mapped genomic region through colinear chaining.

name: nanopore-read-alignment
description: Use when aligning Oxford Nanopore MinION 1d/2d reads (or PacBio reads) to a reference genome with high sensitivity despite high error rates, or when downstream SV/SNV calling requires gapped alignments that span 100 bp–4 kbp insertion/deletion events directly.

name: nanopore-read-alignment
description: Use when ONT long-read FASTQ data (e.g. SQK-PCS111 cDNA, SQK-RNA002 dRNA, or SQK-LSK109 pDNA reads) must be mapped to a plasmid or mRNA reference as the first step of VAX-seq quality analysis.

name: nanopore-read-alignment-and-biotype-assignment
description: Use when you have nanopore DRS reads from a RISER live run (even-numbered channels = deplete, others = control) and need per-transcript or per-biotype read-count and nucleotide-count changes to evaluate depletion/enrichment efficiency.

name: nanopore-read-alignment-and-preprocessing
description: Use when raw ONT reads must be converted into methylation-annotated primary-alignment BAMs (MM/ML tags) plus SNV-phased, haplotagged BAM/VCF inputs for methylation-based phasing of ~30X human autosomes.

name: nanopore-read-alignment-to-grch38
description: Use when Dorado sup-basecalled ONT reads (kit v14, R10.4.1) from samples such as HG002/HG003/HG004 must be placed on GRCh38 as sorted, indexed BAMs before variant calling.

name: nanopore-read-alignment-to-reference-genome
description: Use when raw nanopore PASS reads (e.g. PCR-amplified or M.SssI-treated E. coli K12 samples in fast5/fastq) must be mapped to a reference such as ecoli_k12_mg1655.fasta before methylation-calling or coverage filtering.

name: nanopore-read-anchor-detection
description: Use when a pipeline must convert coarse seed-hit clusters from a seeding stage into precise read/reference coordinate anchors prior to anchor chaining (LCSk), specifically for MinION nanopore or other long error-prone reads.

name: nanopore-read-attribute-parsing
description: Use when a POD5 nanopore file's per-read metadata must be fully enumerated and flattened — e.g. to inspect nested attributes of a selected read ID or export them to per-read JSON files.

name: nanopore-read-basecalling
description: Use when raw nanopore signals simulated from a reference (e.g. BLOW5/POD5 from seq2squiggle, squigulator, or DeepSimulator under R9.4.1 or R10.4.1 chemistry) must be turned into basecalled reads for variant-detection benchmarking.

name: nanopore-read-basecalling-and-resquiggling
description: Use when starting from raw single-read FAST5 Nanopore files (e.g. R9.4 plant reads) that need basecalls and raw-signal-to-reference alignment before deep-learning methylation detection.

name: nanopore-read-basecalling-orchestration
description: Use when raw nanopore signal files (FAST5, .fast5.gz, POD5, .pod5.gz) or already-basecalled FASTQ (.fastq, .fq, .fastq.gz, .fq.gz) must enter VirDetector's preprocessing before taxonomic classification.

name: nanopore-read-classification
description: Use when base-called nanopore reads must be classified as target vs non-target (e.g., adaptive-sampling host/strain depletion) against one-genome or multi-strain pan-genome references where minimap2 alignment is too slow or memory-hungry.

name: nanopore-read-data-preprocessing
description: Use when input data are ONT multi-read fast5 files that must be split into per-read single fast5 files before raw-signal tools like tombo resquiggle can process them.

name: nanopore-read-de-novo-assembly
description: Use when assembling untargeted (metagenomic) Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads from clinical samples where uneven viral genome abundance (e.g., co-infections) may prevent a single Canu run from recovering low-abundance virus genomes.

name: nanopore-read-demultiplexing
description: Use when demultiplexing Nanopore FASTQ reads from barcoding kits (e.g. SQK-RBK114-96 rapid or SQK-NBD114-96 native barcoding), especially when reads show complex barcode attachments, partially trimmed adapter contamination, or custom barcode patterns.

name: nanopore-read-demultiplexing
description: Use when you have dual-indexed MinION FASTA/FASTQ amplicon reads (e.g. long rDNA amplicons) plus a barcode/index combination file and need to assign each read to a specimen by matching forward/reverse barcodes and primers.

name: nanopore-read-demultiplexing
description: Use when nanopore FASTQ/FASTA reads have been ligated with a PRO-designed barcode kit and each read must be assigned to its source barcode, especially when comparing accuracy against Guppy or edit-distance assignment.

name: nanopore-read-downsampling
description: Use when comparing methylation callers or basecalling models on nanopore data and you need standardized, depth-matched BAM inputs (e.g., 10x and 30x coverage) from high-coverage R10.4 datasets.

name: nanopore-read-end-trimming
description: Use when raw Oxford Nanopore FASTQ reads contain PCR/tiling primer and adapter sequences at read ends and a fixed-length trim of both ends is needed before downstream classification or assembly.

name: nanopore-read-error-correction
description: Use when assembling genomes from noisy Oxford Nanopore long reads and you must choose between correct-then-assemble vs assemble-then-correct correction strategies, or when polishing a draft long-read assembly to final accuracy with Illumina short reads.

name: nanopore-read-filtering-statistics-summarization
description: Reference for generating or verifying per-sample output tables (reads.tsv, consensus.tsv, contigs.tsv) and HTML report sections summarizing read filtering statistics from a ViMOP Nextflow run.

name: nanopore-read-haplotype-phasing
description: Use when long nanopore reads must be assigned to a parental haplotype using trio-phased heterozygous SNPs, e.g. to phase SVs or determine parental origin of de novo breakpoint junctions.

name: nanopore-read-haplotype-tagging
description: Use when ONT nanopore reads (e.g., an HG002 R10.4 alignment BAM) must be partitioned into paternal/maternal haplotype read sets for allele-specific methylation analysis and a phased VCF of heterozygous variants is available.

name: nanopore-read-kmer-extraction
description: Use when compressing or indexing ONT nanopore read sequences from a FASTQ file and a k-mer–based MinHash sketch is needed to find reads overlapping a query sequence.

name: nanopore-read-length-statistics
description: Use when characterizing a nanopore WGS dataset by read-length statistics and genome-wide coverage at MAPQ ≥ 20 across alternative aligners (e.g., rebuilding the NA19240 control metrics from Table 2).

name: nanopore-read-library-configuration
description: Use when preparing Fast-SG hybrid scaffolding or assembly runs on raw Nanopore/PacBio long-read FASTA libraries, e.g. shallow ~5X NA12878 ultra-long reads feeding a scaffolding graph built with k-mer size 22.

name: nanopore-read-mapping-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing long-read mapper sensitivity (mapped reads/bases) or consensus accuracy on Oxford Nanopore MinION data against published GraphMap results, or when validating a mapper build on real MinION data sets.

name: nanopore-read-mapping-decision-scoring
description: Use when you have a per-read feature table (read_id, mapping-quality ratio, chain-score ratio, mean chain-score ratio) from RawHash2 output and need to reproduce or audit the weighted-sum mapped/unmapped decision.

name: nanopore-read-mapping-filtering
description: Use when raw nanopore DRS fast5 signals need transcript-level assignment — e.g. before curating training/testing sets for RISER, or before computing per-transcript read/nucleotide counts for enrichment or depletion benchmarks.

name: nanopore-read-metadata-inspection
description: Use when the task requires locating a subset of reads by read ID within one or more POD5 files — e.g. searching read IDs by substring, sorting them lexicographically, or intersecting them with a supplied list of read IDs.

name: nanopore-read-phasing-with-snp-haplotyping
description: Use when ONT reads need to be assigned to parental haplotypes to resolve haplotype-specific methylation — e.g. detecting imprinted control regions, parent-of-origin labeling in a trio, or differential methylation between phases.

name: nanopore-read-preprocessing-and-trimming
description: Use when raw nanopore sequencing files (FASTQ, .fastq.gz, FAST5, or POD5) must be basecalled, preprocessed, and primer-trimmed before viral genome reconstruction or taxonomic classification in VirDetector.

name: nanopore-read-probability-statistical-testing
description: Use when comparing nanopore direct RNA m6A between two conditions (e.g. WT vs knock-out replicates) using per-read modification probabilities to call differentially modified transcriptomic sites.

name: nanopore-read-processing
description: Use when you have untargeted metagenomic nanopore FASTQ data (optionally barcode-demultiplexed into barcode01, barcode02, ... subdirectories) from MinION sequencing of clinical or animal samples and need to detect known viral species and reconstruct their consensus genomes.

name: nanopore-read-quality-filtering
description: Use when running mCaller on ONT eventalign data and read-level noise from low-quality basecalls is degrading per-position methylation accuracy, and you want to restrict classification to reads above an average base-quality threshold.

name: nanopore-read-reference-alignment
description: Use when a viral genome must be reconstructed from nanopore FASTQ reads for which a suitable reference FASTA already exists, e.g. a known virus such as West Nile virus where mapping beats de novo assembly.

name: nanopore-read-resistance-genotyping
description: Use when you have raw single-molecule nanopore (MinION) reads of a bacterial isolate and need antibiotic resistance predictions without prior error correction, ideally benchmarked against a second sequencing platform.

name: nanopore-read-simulation
description: Use when evaluating SV-caller sensitivity/specificity (NanoSV, Lumpy, Sniffles) without wet-lab validation: simulated nanopore reads with a realistic error profile and known ground-truth breakpoints must be generated.

name: nanopore-read-simulation
description: Use when you need ground-truth nanopore read sets of known origin and adjustable accuracy to benchmark read classification or alignment accuracy (F1, precision, recall) and throughput.

name: nanopore-read-simulation-error-modeling
description: Use when benchmarking long-read taxonomic classifiers or ARG host-assignment pipelines and realistic simulated ONT metagenomes with controlled error profiles (HQ vs LQ) and known ground-truth species composition are needed.

name: nanopore-read-subsampling
description: Use when you need to determine how many Nanopore amplicon reads are sufficient for an accurate majority-vote consensus, by sweeping subsample sizes and measuring consensus error against a higher-accuracy reference consensus.

name: nanopore-read-subsampling-coverage-normalization
description: Use when pooled Nanopore FASTQs of uneven depth must be subsampled to a fixed coverage (e.g. 50x or 60x) before assembly benchmarking or fair tool comparison.

name: nanopore-read-subsampling-coverage-scaling
description: Use when assessing the minimum nanopore sequencing depth at which nanoHiMe-seq CpG methylation calls remain accurate versus WGBS, e.g. before committing MinION flowcells for a low-coverage epigenomics experiment.

name: nanopore-read-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when you have untargeted metagenomic nanopore FASTQ reads (e.g. Lassa, Ebola, Dengue clinical samples) and need to remove non-viral reads based on Centrifuge taxonomic classification confidence before viral genome reconstruction.

name: nanopore-read-to-seed-alignment
description: Use when you have FASTA-formatted nanopore reads (e.g. R7.3, R9 1D/2D, R9.4 1D MinION runs) plus a set of pre-selected 'not too repetitive' seed sequences of uniform length, and need read-to-seed alignments to drive a TULIP seed-layout assembly.

name: nanopore-read-until-platform-comparison
description: Use when reported per-read execution time (ms) and energy (mJ) measurements exist for HARU (Xilinx FPGA + 4-core ARM) and one or more software baselines, and the goal is to derive or verify EDP and platform-level efficiency ratios.

name: nanopore-read-variant-calling
description: Use when nanopore reads (e.g. nanoHiMe-seq FASTQ/BAM aligned to hg19) must be assigned to parental alleles — e.g. to compute per-allele phasing rates over H3K4me3/H3K27me3 peaks or CpG islands — and heterozygous variants are available or need calling.

name: nanopore-reference-alignment-parameter-tuning
description: Use when raw multi-fast5 ONT direct RNA reads must be converted to single-read fast5 and raw current signal aligned (resquiggled) to a reference FASTA before per-position modification detection, especially when tuning alignment/event-detection parameters for rRNA or similar references.

name: nanopore-signal-basecalling-and-alignment
description: Use when raw nanopore direct RNA sequencing fast5 files must be assigned transcript identities (e.g., to label RNA classes for model training or quantify transcript abundance) via basecalling, transcriptome mapping, and high-confidence alignment filtering.

name: nanopore-signal-binary-npy-export
description: Use when a single read's raw nanopore current measurements stored in a POD5 file must be extracted into a .npy Numpy binary or plain-text file for downstream numpy processing without the pod5 API.

name: nanopore-signal-classification
description: Use when raw nanopore DRS signals (fast5, RNA002 or RNA004 kits) must be classified into RNA classes such as protein_coding mRNA, mtRNA, lncRNA or globin (HBA1/HBA2/HBB) directly from the first few seconds of signal.

name: nanopore-signal-event-alignment
description: Use when starting from raw nanopore FAST5 files and you need event-level signal-to-reference alignments (test.eventalign.txt) as input for nanoHiMe modification calling or model training.

name: nanopore-signal-event-extraction
description: Use when raw ONT fast5 reads must be resquiggled, converted to multi-fast5, and parsed into position-anchored signal events to support k-mer-level comparisons of native vs WGA samples.

name: nanopore-signal-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw Nanopore FAST5/POD5 reads have been basecalled and re-squiggled against a genome reference and per-base sequence-context plus raw-signal features are needed to train or run a methylation-calling model on cytosine sites.

name: nanopore-signal-inference-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to measure and compare inference/processing throughput (kbp/s) of raw MinION fast5 signal tools or basecalling pipelines across hardware tiers such as a 2GB Jetson Nano versus a high-end desktop.

name: nanopore-signal-methylation-calling
description: Use when raw ONT signal data (POD5 or FAST5) from R9.4.1 or R10.4.1 flowcells must be basecalled, aligned, and analyzed for CpG 5mC methylation at per-read or per-site resolution, or benchmarked against short-read/microarray ground truth.

name: nanopore-signal-methylation-calling
description: Use when you need to detect methylated CpG sites from basecalled Nanopore reads (FASTQ/BAM) plus raw FAST5 signal data on a CUDA GPU, and prioritize end-to-end execution time versus CPU-only tools.

name: nanopore-signal-methylation-prediction
description: Use when you have nanopore DRS FAST5/eventaligned signals (e.g. HEK293 WT, HeLa, IVT controls) and need single-molecule m6A/m5C calls, site-level probabilities, or stoichiometry in any sequence context without a KO/control sample.

name: nanopore-signal-preprocessing
description: Use when raw DRS FAST5 data has been basecalled (Guppy 4.0.11+), aligned (minimap2, samtools -F 232457), and eventaligned (Nanopolish --scale-events), and per-read 9-mer signal inputs are needed for CHEUI Model 1.

name: nanopore-signal-preprocessing-adapter-polya-trimming
description: Use when raw nanopore DRS fast5 signals (RNA002/R9.4.1) must have the adapter and poly(A) stall trimmed before basecalling (e.g., Chiron/Dorado) or before feeding fixed-length inputs to a signal classifier such as RISER.

name: nanopore-signal-read-classification
description: Use when input is raw ONT fast5 signal data (amplified or metagenomic 16S) and you need per-read target-species detection on inexpensive hardware without basecalling, e.g. MinION as a species detector.

name: nanopore-signal-resquiggle
description: Use when raw (uncorrected) Nanopore FAST5 reads must have their electrical signals aligned to genome-reference bases before signal-based methylation calling, e.g. prior to deepsignal_plant call_mods.

name: nanopore-signal-resquiggling
description: Use when raw nanopore fast5 signal must be aligned to a reference genome and reformatted to multi-fast5 before running methylation motif callers such as Snapper's sample-vs-WGA comparison.

name: nanopore-signal-resquiggling-against-transcriptome
description: Use when raw Nanopore direct RNA sequencing FAST5 files must be basecalled, re-squiggled, and aligned to a reference transcriptome to produce signal-mapped reads for downstream per-site feature extraction (e.g. RedNano m6A detection).

name: nanopore-signal-simulation
description: Use when synthetic ONT R10.4.1 DNA or RNA004 direct-RNA read signals (POD5) are needed to benchmark basecalling accuracy, variant calling, assembly, or simulator fidelity without real sequencing runs.

name: nanopore-signal-zscore-normalization
description: Use when preparing raw nanopore signal reads (e.g., BLOW5 format from R9.4 chemistry) for signal-domain alignment such as sDTW-based Read Until, where events must be normalized and cast to 16-bit fixed point before dispatch to an accelerator.

name: nanopore-simulated-read-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing untargeted nanopore virus genome pipelines for robustness to high mutation levels or evaluating recovery of partial genomes below 50% completeness on simulated read sets.

name: nanopore-snp-calling-and-polishing
description: Use when assembling Nanopore R9/R10 diploid datasets with PECAT, when corrected reads alone give insufficient SNP calls for phasing, or when Nanopore assemblies require post-assembly polishing before evaluation.

name: nanopore-snp-detection-filtering
description: Use when MinION amplicon or whole-genome reads (FASTA/FASTQ) must be mapped to a reference and candidate SNPs called with explicit coverage thresholds, e.g., targeted Plasmodium falciparum or EGFR amplicon resequencing.

name: nanopore-squiggle-dtw-alignment-execution
description: Use when raw nanopore signal data in BLOW5 format must be aligned to a reference genome in the signal (squiggle) domain for Read Until / adaptive sampling, especially when real-time performance on resource-constrained devices is the goal.

name: nanopore-squiggle-mapping
description: Use when raw nanopore signal reads in BLOW5 format must be aligned directly against a reference genome at the signal level for Read Until / adaptive sampling decisions, especially when basecalling is too slow or resource-intensive.

name: nanopore-structural-variant-calling
description: Use when long-read PromethION/nanopore WGS reads must be turned into a merged SV call set (DEL/DUP/INS/INV/TRA) and when large CNVs >50 kb or coverage-supported polishing of caller output is the goal.

name: nanopore-structural-variant-qc
description: Use when a raw NanoSV VCF from nanopore data (e.g. NA12878 chr1) needs stringent post-calling filtering before downstream comparison, phasing, or benchmarking.

name: nanopore-sv-call-set-qc
description: Use when a raw NanoSV VCF from MinION long-read data (tens of thousands of SV calls) must be reduced to a high-confidence SV set and intermediate/final call counts must match published checkpoints.

name: nanopore-sv-calling
description: Use when calling structural variants (deletions, inversions, translocations) from long nanopore reads at medium coverage (11–16×), or when reproducing the NanoSV SV discovery workflow from Cretu Stancu et al. 2017.

name: nanopore-translocation-time-novelty-detection
description: Use when ONT nanopore FAST5 reads (e.g. NA12878 / SRR15058166) must be converted to per-base translocation times and scored for non-B DNA novelty against motif-free B-DNA controls at an FDR-controlled level.

name: nanopore-vs-bisulfite-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing nanopore methylation calls to whole-genome BS-seq in repetitive or centromeric regions, to quantify the fraction of CHH sites profiled by each method at a minimum read-coverage threshold.

name: nanopore-vs-bisulfite-cross-platform-comparison
description: Use when comparing CpG site coverage between nanopore modification-call outputs (tsv with read_id, chromosome, pos_in_strand, strand, methylation_rate) and matched BS-seq calls across matched human or plant whole-genome datasets.

name: nanopore-wgbs-cross-platform-benchmarking
description: Use when you have per-site methylation frequency files from nanopore tools and matched WGBS frequencies and need to test whether sequence context (k-mer around CpG) explains nanopore-WGBS disagreement.

name: nanopore-wgbs-methylation-correlation-analysis
description: Use when nanopore per-site methylation frequency tables (augmented BED format) must be compared to matched WGBS methylation frequencies across coverage thresholds (1x–20x) to verify concordance stability.

name: nanopore-wgs-dataset-acquisition
description: Use when a workflow needs the raw nanopore WGS reads (e.g. ENA accessions ERR2585112/ERR2585115 from PRJEB26791, NA19240 PromethION) as FASTQ input for alignment-based HLA-I/II prediction or similar long-read benchmarking.

name: nanopore-wgs-read-streaming
description: Use when a whole-genome shotgun long-read FASTQ (e.g. Oxford Nanopore PromethION WGS) needs HLA class I/II allele prediction, and disk/time-efficient single-command streaming of aligner output into HLAminer is preferred over writing SAM files to disk.

name: nanoprd
description: Turn a product idea into an executable plan. Produces project context, a PRD, an architecture document, and a set of nanotasks - atomic, doable tasks, one user-observable behavior each, small enough for a coding agent to pick up and finish in a single pass. name: neqsim-advanced-control-mpc-and-virtual-sensing
description: Guides agents through ProcessLinkedMPC, ProcessLinearizer, ModelPredictiveController, VirtualFlowMeter, SoftSensor, and DataReconciliationEngine. USE WHEN: identifying a process model for MPC, exporting state-space or industrial controller models, estimating unmetered flow or properties, checking controller structures, detecting steady state, reconciling noisy measurements, or screening controller performance.

name: neqsim-ageing-life-extension-screening
description: Educational ageing-trend and remaining-life screening (Laplace test, Crow-AMSAA fit, failure projection, maintain-vs-replace) plus the installation technical life basis (design life, cut-off, life-limiting populations). USE WHEN: asked whether equipment ages, how long a host or installation can operate, or whether a study horizon fits technical life.

name: neqsim-agent-handoff
description: Agent-to-agent communication schema for NeqSim. USE WHEN: composing multi-agent pipelines where one agent's output feeds another agent's input. Defines structured result formats for fluid definitions, simulation results, and design outputs that agents can pass to each other.

name: neqsim-agentic-process-optimization
description: Agentic closed-loop optimization of large multi-area NeqSim ProcessModel plants with convergence gating and equipment introspection. USE WHEN: an agent must optimize a live full-plant flowsheet (setpoints, compressor pressures, heater temperatures, routing fractions) across years/scenarios with surge/RVP/spec constraints and per-trial feasibility gating. Covers getAdjustableParameters, runUntilConverged, RunStatus, getOperatingPoint surge margins, RVP, copy() sweeps.

name: neqsim-anp-open-data
description: Reads Brazilian ANP open data: bid-round blocks, field and well production, well data bank, GeoANP layers (blocks, fields, wells, gas pipelines), installation positions from wellheads and tie-in host ranking, with CRS, unit and date checks. USE WHEN: a task needs Brazilian block, field or well facts, a host such as a pre-salt FPSO, nearby installations or export lines for a tie-in, or a Sodir-like open-data basis.

name: neqsim-anp-well-production-history
description: Reads Brazilian ANP well-level production open data into unit-explicit series: merges onshore, offshore and pre-salt files without double counting, builds well/field histories with GOR and water cut, checks data features, prepares decline-fit input and a declared fluid basis. USE WHEN: a task needs production history of Brazilian wells or fields, decline or GOR analysis, a fluid basis from public data, or what public data can support for an MBAL or well-flow model.

name: neqsim-api-patterns
description: NeqSim Java/Python API patterns for fluids, flashes, process equipment and units. USE WHEN: selecting EOS/mixing-rule selection and property retrieval, including viscosity, thermal conductivity, binary/effective diffusion, gas-oil-water interfacial tension and black-oil PVT table conversion. Follow linked references for exact model selection, initialization and tested examples.

name: neqsim-artificial-lift-screening
description: Educational artificial-lift screening that compares a simple straight-line IPR natural deliverability against a target rate and screens gas lift and ESP feasibility from a required bottomhole-pressure reduction. USE WHEN: a task needs a public, screening-level recommendation of natural flow, gas lift, or ESP for a well before detailed inflow/outflow (nodal) analysis and lift design.

name: neqsim-asset-value-npv-screening
description: Educational discounted-cash-flow (DCF) asset-value screening that builds a year-by-year net cash flow from revenue, OPEX, and a CAPEX schedule and returns NPV, IRR, and payback with a simple flat tax. USE WHEN: a task needs a public, screening-level NPV/IRR/payback before detailed NeqSim field-development economics or qualified commercial review.

name: neqsim-autonomous-investigation
description: Autonomous observe-hypothesize-predict-test-discriminate loop for operational anomalies. USE WHEN: solving a PEPR action, root-cause or operational study where the symptom, driver or important relationships are NOT given up front. Uses neqsim.process.diagnostics.RelationshipGraph for lead-lag relationship discovery across historian tags, then hands off to neqsim-root-cause-analysis.

name: neqsim-bathymetry-profile-screening
description: Educational bathymetry profile screening from supplied soundings. USE WHEN: a task needs public, screening-level seabed depth interpolation along a route, slope screening, and steep-section flags from sounding points before detailed free-span and on-bottom-stability design.

name: neqsim-benchmark-reference-data
description: Reproducible, source-traceable benchmark validation for NeqSim tasks: a registry of reference sources with authority tiers and uncertainties (IAPWS, Span-Wagner, GERG-2008, CoolProp, NIST), an offline anchor table, PASS/WARN/FAIL grading with the three-point minimum, and the benchmark_validation block the report and CI gate consume. USE WHEN: validating NeqSim against independent data, writing a benchmark notebook or block, tracing a deviation to a citable source, or checking a benchmark claim.

name: neqsim-brazil-offshore-infrastructure-market
description: Public data and helpers for Brazilian offshore (Santos and Campos pre-salt) gas export routes, processing plants, tariff status, third-party access, gas spec, oil marketing and host capacity, with explicit UNKNOWNs and source ids. USE WHEN: a Brazilian block or tie-back evaluation needs gas export, CO2 removal, wellhead net-back, host ullage or market context, and no numeric offshore tariff is public.

name: neqsim-brazil-presalt-analogue-basis
description: Declared best-guess fluid and flow-assurance basis for Santos Basin pre-salt blocks when no PVT exists: analogue ranges, CO2-rich gas handling, material and EOS checks, and an assumption register. USE WHEN: a frontier block in Santos or Campos pre-salt must be evaluated, a CO2-rich associated gas or CO2 re-injection case is in play, or a near-field analogue fluid is needed.
